people.label: Charles I. Halt
people.sub: Lt Col USAF (later Col); Deputy Base Commander, RAF Bentwaters/Woodbridge 1980-81
people.narrative: Halt wrote the single most consequential UFO document ever produced by a serving US officer inside a NATO nuclear-capable installation. On 13 January 1981, as Deputy Base Commander of the 81st Combat Support Group at RAF Bentwaters/Woodbridge, he sent a one-page memorandum captioned 'Unexplained Lights' to the RAF station commander describing events of 26-28 December 1980: security patrolmen encountering a 'strange glowing object' that was 'metalic in appearance and triangular in shape, approximately two to three meters across the base'; three ground depressions 1.5 inches deep and 7 inches in diameter; and radiation readings of 0.1 milliroentgens beta/gamma peaking in the depressions. The memo is not a UFO buff's account - it is an official USAF memorandum, released to the public through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense FOIA office and re-released under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677 in September 1997. Halt personally led the 28 December patrol and tape-recorded it. He remained in the Air Force for another decade, retiring as a full colonel, and only after retirement began stating publicly that he believed the objects were under intelligent control and that base personnel had been debriefed under pressure. In 2010 he executed a notarized affidavit asserting that the objects were not of terrestrial origin and that USAF and UK authorities had worked to suppress the incident; he has since stated that airmen were subjected to what he characterized as drugged and hypnotic debriefings. The 45-year documentary life of the Halt memo is a case study in the board's central thesis: the record exists, it was written by the responsible officer at the time, and the institutional response has been to route it into a category ('unexplained lights') that requires no follow-up.
people.tierRationale: Tier A: the author of a contemporaneous, FOIA-released official USAF memorandum documenting a physical-trace event at a nuclear-weapons-capable NATO base, who has since gone on the record under oath-equivalent affidavit.

people.label: James W. Penniston
people.sub: USAF SSgt, 81st Security Police Squadron; first responder, Rendlesham 26 Dec 1980
people.narrative: Penniston was the senior security police NCO who went outside the RAF Woodbridge east gate in the early hours of 26 December 1980. His contemporaneous notebook - later released by him and reproduced by researchers - contains sketches and the phrase 'craft of unknown origin.' He has stated on the record that he approached the object, walked around it, and physically touched a warm, glass-smooth surface bearing raised symbols, and that he and John Burroughs were subsequently subjected to lengthy debriefings by personnel he could not identify. He signed an official USAF witness statement in January 1981 which, in its released form, is markedly less detailed than his notebook. The gap between the notebook and the official statement is the evidentiary point: it is a documented instance of a first-hand military account being compressed as it moved up the chain, in exactly the manner the concealment thesis predicts. Penniston's later claims - including a binary-code download experienced during the encounter - have made him easier to dismiss, which is itself a familiar pattern in this record: the most exposed witnesses accumulate the most discrediting material.

people.label: John Burroughs

people.narrative: Burroughs matters less for what he saw than for what happened when he tried to get his own medical file. He was one of the airmen at the east gate on 26 December 1980. Decades later, suffering a cardiac condition, he sought Department of Veterans Affairs disability benefits and needed his December 1980-January 1981 service medical records to establish an in-service exposure. He and his counsel reported that the records could not be produced, and the case became a multi-year administrative fight that ran through congressional offices - Senator John McCain's staff among them - before the VA granted him service-connected benefits in 2015. The VA's grant did not adjudicate what he encountered; it adjudicated that something happened in service. That is the load-bearing fact. The Burroughs matter converts Rendlesham from a sightings story into a records story: a US government department paid a claim that turns on an event the Air Force has never formally acknowledged, while the medical documentation from the relevant window was not available through normal channels. Missing records with no destruction authority is the same signature GAO found in the Roswell files in 1995.

people.label: Paul Frederick Bennewitz
people.sub: Physicist; president, Thunder Scientific Corp.; target of AFOSI disinformation 1980-1988
people.narrative: Bennewitz is the clearest documented casualty of a US counterintelligence operation run against an American civilian over UFO information. He was a working physicist who ran Thunder Scientific Corporation, an instrumentation firm whose customers included the Air Force, from a property whose sightlines took in the Manzano Weapons Storage Area and Coyote Canyon on the eastern edge of Kirtland AFB. From 1979 he recorded lights and electronic signals over the Manzano nuclear-weapons storage complex and reported them - to the Air Force, in writing, repeatedly. The Air Force's documented response was an AFOSI file: a formal AFOSI complaint-form record dated 10 November 1980 confirming that Kirtland security police had observed unexplained aerial objects over Coyote Canyon and that Bennewitz's photography and reporting were under official notice. What followed, on the accounts of the AFOSI personnel involved, was not an investigation but a feed: Bennewitz was supplied with fabricated material about underground alien bases, treaties and biological experiments, calibrated to his existing beliefs, in order to discredit him and to mask whatever it was he had actually recorded near a nuclear storage site. He deteriorated, was hospitalised for psychiatric care in 1988, and died in 2003. The Bennewitz affair is the template: the state does not need to seize a witness's evidence if it can destroy the witness's credibility, and it can do that using its own personnel, on the record, with no legal consequence.
people.tierRationale: Tier A: the disinformation operation against him is attested by the participating AFOSI agent on the record and anchored in a dated AFOSI document about unexplained objects over Kirtland's nuclear storage area.

people.narrative: Doty is the only US counterintelligence officer to have stated on camera and on the record that he personally ran disinformation about UFOs against American civilians as part of his official duties. As an AFOSI special agent at Kirtland AFB from 1979, he authored or handled the 1980-1983 Kirtland documents concerning unexplained objects over Coyote Canyon, fed fabricated material to Paul Bennewitz, and in April 1983 showed the documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe a briefing paper purporting to describe a government programme - the 'Project Aquarius' teletype - which she was not permitted to copy. He left AFOSI in 1988 and later served as a New Mexico State Police officer; his 321-page state police personnel file was obtained under the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act and published in 2021, giving the first full documentary picture of his post-Air Force career. Doty's value to this board is not that his statements are reliable - they are not, and he has repeatedly changed them - but that his existence is the proof of concept. people.label: William L. Moore
people.sub: UFO researcher and author; co-author 'The Roswell Incident' (1980); AFOSI collaborator
people.narrative: Moore is the hinge between the Roswell revival, the MJ-12 documents and the AFOSI disinformation programme - and he confessed to the last of those himself. With Charles Berlitz he published 'The Roswell Incident' in 1980, the book that pulled the 1947 event back into public circulation after three decades. In December 1984 his associate Jaime Shandera received an anonymous roll of undeveloped 35mm film containing what became known as the Eisenhower Briefing Document of Operation Majestic-12. Moore and Shandera controlled the release of that material for the next several years. Then, at the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas in July 1989, Moore told the assembled UFO community that he had worked with Air Force counterintelligence, that he had passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz on their behalf, and that he had done so in exchange for access. It was, in its way, the most honest act in the field: a researcher publicly conceding he had been run. Everything downstream of Moore - MJ-12's provenance, the Aquarius material, the Bennewitz collapse - has to be read through the fact that the principal civilian channel was in contact with the counterintelligence service the material was supposedly about. That does not make the material false. It makes its origin an intelligence question rather than a research question.

people.label: Jaime H. Shandera

people.narrative: Shandera was a Los Angeles television producer working with Bill Moore when, on 11 December 1984, an unmarked envelope postmarked Albuquerque arrived at his home containing a roll of undeveloped 35mm black-and-white film. Developed, it showed eight pages: a briefing document dated 18 November 1952 prepared for President-elect Eisenhower on 'Operation Majestic-12,' listing twelve named officials and describing the recovery of a crashed disc and four bodies near Roswell. The Albuquerque postmark is the detail that will not go away - it points at the same city and the same window as the AFOSI Kirtland operation against Bennewitz. Shandera, Moore and Stanton Friedman held the material for two and a half years, made a National Archives search that produced the Cutler-Twining memorandum in 1985, and released the package publicly in May 1987. Shandera died in 2019. His role is that of the receiving end of a channel: whoever sent that film chose a producer with a documented connection to a researcher with a documented connection to AFOSI.

people.label: Harold E. Puthoff
people.sub: Physicist; founder of SRI's CIA-funded psychoenergetics programme 1972-1985; later NIDS, TTSA, Sol Foundation
people.narrative: Puthoff is the single continuous thread running from the 1970s intelligence-funded fringe programmes to the 2017 disclosure wave. In 1972 he began, at Stanford Research Institute, a programme of experiments in what CIA's Office of Technical Service funded as psychoenergetics - the work that became GRILL FLAME, CENTER LANE, SUN STREAK and finally STARGATE across CIA, Army INSCOM and DIA. He and Russell Targ published in Nature in October 1974, an extraordinary placement for classified-adjacent work, and his 1978 SRI paper 'Standard Remote Viewing Protocol (Local Targets)' survives in the declassified STARGATE corpus - roughly 12,000 pages CIA released in 1995 after the American Institutes for Research evaluation and the programme's transfer and termination. The point for this board is not whether remote viewing worked. It is that Puthoff spent thirteen years as the civilian principal investigator of a compartmented US intelligence programme run through a private research institute, with agency funding, agency taskings and agency security. He then did exactly the same thing again: consultant to Robert Bigelow's National Institute for Discovery Science from 1995, principal investigator of the Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies contract work under AAWSAP from 2008, and co-founder of To The Stars Academy in 2017. The pattern - government money, private vehicle, no acknowledgement - is the pattern this board is cataloguing, and Puthoff has been inside it for fifty years.

people.label: Robert T. Bigelow

people.narrative: Bigelow privatised the problem. A Las Vegas real-estate developer who built the Budget Suites of America extended-stay chain, he founded the National Institute for Discovery Science in 1995 as a privately funded research institute studying aerial phenomena, animal mutilations and related anomalies, and staffed it with people carrying federal clearances and federal programme histories - Hal Puthoff from the CIA/DIA remote-viewing programmes, Colonel John Alexander from Army INSCOM and Los Alamos, the biochemist Colm Kelleher, and Jacques Vallee. people.label: John B. Alexander

people.narrative: Alexander is the retired Army colonel who spent the late 1980s trying to find the UFO programme from inside the government, with credentials that should have worked, and reported that he could not find it. What his account does establish is that the search happened, that it was conducted by cleared senior people, and that the answer they got was the same answer David Grusch got in 2019: the programme, if it exists, does not answer to people who ask through channels. people.label: Steven M. Greer
people.sub: Emergency physician; founder of CSETI (1990) and the Disclosure Project (1993); National Press Club event 9 May 2001
people.narrative: Greer built the first mass witness-aggregation project and demonstrated both its power and its limits. A practising emergency physician, he founded the Center for the Study of Extraterrestrial Intelligence in 1990 and the Disclosure Project in 1993 with the explicit aim of assembling former military and government personnel willing to testify to Congress. On 9 May 2001 he convened roughly twenty of them at the National Press Club in Washington - radar operators, missile launch officers, air traffic controllers, FAA personnel - and announced that more than four hundred had given testimony, demanding congressional hearings with subpoena power and amnesty for witnesses. The event drew heavy international coverage and produced no hearing. Its consequence for the record is twofold. First, it created a large videotaped corpus of named former personnel making specific, dated, on-the-record claims, some of which - notably the missile-facility shutdown accounts - align with the FOIA-released overflight documents from 1975. Second, Greer's subsequent trajectory into claims that outran his evidence gave the institutions he was pressuring a durable reason to treat the whole category as unserious. The Clinton White House's own UFO FOIA collection (2006-0474-F) consists in the majority of documents Greer sent it, which is a precise measure of how the material was received: filed as correspondence.

people.label: Eric W. Davis
people.sub: Astrophysicist; EarthTech/Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin; NIDS; BAASS; author of the Wilson notes
people.narrative: Davis is the author of the single most specific document in the modern record about a denied programme. An astrophysicist working with Hal Puthoff at EarthTech and the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, he was a NIDS staff scientist, later a BAASS contractor producing Defense Intelligence Reference Documents for AAWSAP, and later still a contractor with The Aerospace Corporation. On 16 October 2002 he met Vice Admiral Thomas R. Wilson - by then recently retired as Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency - reportedly at an EG&G facility in Las Vegas, and made fifteen pages of handwritten notes of what Wilson told him. The notes describe Wilson, while J-2 on the Joint Staff in 1997, learning of a special access programme holding recovered material of non-human origin in the custody of an aerospace contractor, seeking access, and being refused by the programme's security officers on the grounds that he lacked need-to-know - a refusal Wilson is recorded as saying was backed by a contractor programme manager and a lawyer. The notes surfaced publicly in 2019, apparently from material connected to the estate of Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell. Davis has confirmed to journalists that the notes are his. Wilson denies the meeting and the contents. The board records both: the notes are a real artefact whose author is identified and living, and the denial is a real artefact whose author is identified and living. What makes the document structurally important is that its central allegation - a general officer with the highest clearances being refused access by contractor gatekeepers - is the same allegation, twenty-one years earlier, that David Grusch made under oath in July 2023.

entities.label: Project MOON DUST
entities.sub: USAF/State Dept recovery and exploitation program
entities.desc: MOON DUST was the US Air Force codeword for the collection and exploitation of objects and debris of unknown origin that survived re-entry - nominally Soviet and other foreign space hardware, in practice an all-source recovery capability with a standing tasking to acquire material that fell from the sky. It ran from the early 1960s under Air Force Intelligence, with State Department reporting channels supporting the overseas collection, and it is documented in released Department of State cable traffic, one file of which was declassified by CIA. Its significance for this board is jurisdictional rather than evidential: MOON DUST establishes that from at least 1961 the United States maintained a named, funded, worldwide programme whose purpose was to go and get whatever came down, with a chain of custody that ran into Air Force technical intelligence at Wright-Patterson - the same institutional address that the Twining memorandum used in 1947. The Air Force told Congress and researchers for years that MOON DUST had nothing to do with unidentified objects; the programme's own charter language on unidentified fallen material is why that answer never held. MOON DUST and its air-transport twin BLUE FLY are the connective tissue between the Blue Book era and everything that follows: Blue Book was the public-facing sighting file; MOON DUST was the retrieval function, and it did not close in 1969.

entities.label: Operation BLUE FLY

entities.desc: BLUE FLY was the airlift and quick-reaction arm attached to MOON DUST: the standing arrangement by which recovered material of unknown origin was moved, on priority, to Air Force technical intelligence at Foreign Technology Division, Wright-Patterson AFB. Where MOON DUST was the collection authority, BLUE FLY was the transport and custody mechanism. The two names appear together in Air Force intelligence correspondence and in congressional correspondence generated when members of Congress - including New Mexico's delegation in the 1990s - asked the Air Force to explain them. The Air Force's answers shifted over time from denying the programmes existed to conceding they existed but concerned only foreign space debris. For a board tracking custody, BLUE FLY is the most important single word in the 1960s-1980s record: it names the pipeline. Any recovered material entering US custody in that period had a designated route, and that route terminated at Wright-Patterson, which is precisely where the 1947-era chain also terminated and where the Air Force's own 1985 public fact sheet felt it necessary to state that 'there are not now nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.'

entities.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
entities.sub: Documented unidentified incursions over nuclear weapons and missile installations, Oct-Nov 1975
entities.desc: Between late October and mid-November 1975 a sequence of unidentified aerial incursions was documented over Strategic Air Command installations holding nuclear weapons: Loring AFB in Maine on 27-28 October, Wurtsmith AFB in Michigan on 30 October, Malmstrom AFB in Montana and its Minuteman missile fields in early November, and Minot AFB in North Dakota. These were not public sighting reports. They were logged in NORAD and command-post message traffic, generated security alerts, and prompted the launch of interceptors. Six years after the Air Force closed Project Blue Book and told the public that unidentified objects posed no threat to national security, its own operational reporting shows unidentified objects loitering over nuclear weapons storage and Minuteman launch facilities, and F-106 interceptors unable to acquire them. The Malmstrom records were released by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense under FOIA case 97-F-1677 - the same case that released the Halt memo. The 1975 wave is the strongest single refutation of the post-Blue Book official position, and it is entirely built from the government's own operational documents rather than from witness accounts.

entities.label: Rendlesham Forest Incident, RAF Woodbridge/Bentwaters
entities.sub: 26-28 December 1980; USAF-occupied NATO base, Suffolk, England
entities.desc: Over three nights at the end of December 1980, US Air Force personnel at the twin bases of RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters in Suffolk - then a nuclear-capable USAF installation under NATO command - reported an object in the adjacent forest and lights in the sky. The deputy base commander documented it in an official memorandum two weeks later. Three distinct evidentiary layers exist: Lt Col Charles Halt's 13 January 1981 memorandum with its physical-trace and radiation readings; Halt's own live audio recording made during the 28 December patrol; and the signed witness statements of the airmen, including SSgt James Penniston and A1C John Burroughs. The UK Ministry of Defence's contemporaneous position was that the events were of no defence significance, a conclusion reached without interviewing the American witnesses. The incident's later history is the more important part for this board: the memo was released under US FOIA in 1983 before the MoD acknowledged its own file; John Burroughs' US Department of Veterans Affairs claim in the 2010s ran into the unavailability of his service medical records for the relevant period and was ultimately granted; and Halt executed a notarized affidavit in 2010 asserting suppression. Rendlesham is the best-documented case in the world of a physical-trace event at a nuclear-capable NATO installation, and the official position remains that nothing of defence significance occurred.

entities.sub: Air Force Office of Special Investigations records, District 17
entities.desc: The AFOSI file generated at Kirtland Air Force Base beginning in 1980 is the documentary spine of the Bennewitz affair. Its central record - a complaint-form entry dated 10 November 1980 - documents that Kirtland security police observed unexplained aerial objects over the Coyote Canyon and Manzano Weapons Storage Area, the nuclear-weapons storage complex on the base's eastern edge, and notes the reporting and photographic activity of the Albuquerque physicist Paul Bennewitz. The file matters for two independent reasons. First, it is an official Air Force counterintelligence concession that unidentified objects were seen over a nuclear weapons storage site in 1980, eleven years after the Air Force publicly stopped investigating such things. Second, it is the entry point of an operation: the agent associated with the file, Richard Doty, subsequently supplied Bennewitz with fabricated material, showed a purported classified briefing paper to the documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe, and was linked to the channel through which the MJ-12 material reached Bill Moore and Jaime Shandera. The file has never been the subject of any published official review. AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report Volume I does not mention Kirtland, AFOSI, Bennewitz or Doty.

entities.label: Project AQUARIUS (alleged)
entities.sub: Purported USG UFO program named in AFOSI-sourced material, 1983
entities.desc: AQUARIUS is the name attached to a typed paper that AFOSI Special Agent Richard Doty showed the documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe at Kirtland AFB in April 1983, which she was permitted to read and take notes on but not to copy. The paper described a US government programme covering retrieved craft and biological entities, and Howe was told film footage would be released to her for an HBO documentary; it never was, and the project collapsed. A version of the AQUARIUS text later circulated as a teletype and became entangled with the MJ-12 corpus. No copy from any government archive has ever surfaced. The National Archives has stated that it searched the National Security Council's Policy Paper and Meeting Minute indexes under, among other subjects, 'Aquarius' - and found nothing. timeline.label: MOON DUST / BLUE FLY stood up
timeline.text: The Air Force establishes a named worldwide capability to collect and exploit unidentified objects and debris surviving re-entry, with a quick-reaction airlift arm routing material to technical intelligence at Wright-Patterson.

timeline.label: Project Blue Book terminated
timeline.text: The Secretary of the Air Force announces the closure of Blue Book on the finding that no UFO 'has ever given any indication of threat to our national security.' The retrieval function is not announced as closing.

timeline.label: CIA funds SRI psychoenergetics
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin CIA-funded remote-viewing research at Stanford Research Institute - the start of a 23-year compartmented programme in a publicly ridiculed domain.

timeline.label: Targ and Puthoff publish in Nature
timeline.text: 'Information transmission under conditions of sensory shielding' appears in Nature vol. 251, pp. 602-607 - the open-literature face of a classified programme.

timeline.label: Loring AFB overflights begin
timeline.text: Unidentified aerial incursions are logged over Loring AFB, Maine, opening a three-week sequence across SAC nuclear installations.

timeline.label: Malmstrom AFB and Minuteman fields overflown
timeline.text: DoD records later released under FOIA case 97-F-1677 describe numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom AFB and its missile fields, which multiple F-106 interceptors could not acquire.

timeline.label: CAUS founded
timeline.text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy is established under attorney Peter Gersten and begins FOIA litigation against the CIA.

timeline.label: GRILL FLAME formalised
timeline.text: Army INSCOM and DIA formalise operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using SRI methodology - the first of four codenames for one continuous seventeen-year effort.

timeline.label: CAUS sues NSA
timeline.text: Civil Action No. 80-1562 is filed. NSA locates UFO-related records, withholds them, and defends the withholding with a classified affidavit by its Chief of Policy, Eugene Yeates.

timeline.label: AFOSI Kirtland record on Coyote Canyon
timeline.text: An AFOSI document records Kirtland AFB security police observing unexplained aerial objects over the Coyote Canyon / Manzano Weapons Storage Area, and notes Paul Bennewitz's reporting and photography.

timeline.label: Rendlesham Forest incident begins
timeline.text: USAF security patrolmen at the RAF Woodbridge east gate report lights descending into the forest; three enter on foot and report a metallic triangular object.

timeline.label: Halt signs the 'Unexplained Lights' memo
timeline.text: The deputy base commander documents the object, three ground depressions and beta/gamma readings of 0.1 milliroentgens in an official memorandum to the RAF station commander.

timeline.label: D.C. Circuit affirms NSA withholding
timeline.text: The court of appeals affirms judgment for NSA on the basis of an affidavit the plaintiffs were never permitted to see.

timeline.label: Supreme Court denies certiorari
timeline.text: The withholding of UFO-related signals intelligence becomes settled law. The government's position has never been that the records do not exist.

timeline.label: Doty shows Howe the AQUARIUS paper
timeline.text: AFOSI Special Agent Richard Doty shows documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe a purported government briefing paper at Kirtland AFB. She may read but not copy it; the promised film footage never materialises.

timeline.label: CUFON goes online
timeline.text: The Computer UFO Network begins publishing full-text FOIA releases electronically from Seattle, establishing the document-with-case-number standard of evidence.

timeline.label: MJ-12 film arrives postmarked Albuquerque
timeline.text: An anonymous roll of undeveloped 35mm film reaches Jaime Shandera in Los Angeles, containing the purported 1952 Eisenhower briefing on Operation Majestic-12 - mailed from the city where the AFOSI operation was running.

timeline.label: USAF fact sheet denies Wright-Patterson holdings
timeline.text: Wright-Patterson's public affairs office states: 'There are not now nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.'

timeline.label: Remote viewing transfers to DIA as SUN STREAK
timeline.text: The programme moves from Army INSCOM to the Defense Intelligence Agency - the same agency that will contract BAASS twenty-two years later.

timeline.label: MJ-12 documents released publicly
timeline.text: Moore, Shandera and Friedman publish the material. NARA's subsequent searches produce nothing but a single problematic memorandum in Record Group 341.

timeline.label: Bennewitz hospitalised
timeline.text: After eight years of fabricated material fed to him through AFOSI channels, Paul Bennewitz is hospitalised for psychiatric care and withdraws from the field.

timeline.label: Moore admits the AFOSI collaboration
timeline.text: At the MUFON symposium Bill Moore tells the UFO community that he worked with Air Force counterintelligence and knowingly passed disinformation to Bennewitz in exchange for access.

timeline.label: Rockefeller Initiative begins
timeline.text: Laurance Rockefeller begins funding a coordinated campaign to obtain presidential declassification of US government UFO holdings.

timeline.label: Rep. Schiff directs GAO to search the records
timeline.text: After DoD refers his Roswell inquiry to the National Archives rather than answering it, Representative Steven Schiff orders a government-wide GAO records audit.

timeline.label: 'The Best Available Evidence' distributed
timeline.text: Marie Galbraith's Rockefeller-funded briefing document goes to legislators, senior officials and heads of state. No policy response follows.

timeline.label: GAO: Roswell records destroyed, authority unknown
timeline.text: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 finds RAAF administrative records (Mar 1945-Dec 1949) and outgoing messages (Oct 1946-Dec 1949) destroyed, with the disposition form recording neither who destroyed them nor under what authority.

timeline.label: Clintons visit Rockefeller's JY Ranch
timeline.text: The President and First Lady visit Laurance Rockefeller in Jackson, Wyoming - documented in Clinton Library FOIA collection 2006-0546-F, and the occasion on which Rockefeller is reported to have pressed the disclosure case directly.

timeline.label: STARGATE declassified and terminated
timeline.text: CIA releases roughly 12,000 pages of the remote-viewing programme record and the effort is closed - the one case where a compartmented programme in a ridiculed domain was fully documented after the fact.

timeline.label: NIDS founded
timeline.text: Robert Bigelow establishes the National Institute for Discovery Science in Las Vegas and hires Puthoff, Alexander, Kelleher, Vallee and Davis - the cleared cadre that DIA will contract thirteen years later.

timeline.label: Bigelow buys Skinwalker Ranch
timeline.text: The 480-acre Sherman property in Uintah County, Utah is purchased with a condition that the sellers keep quiet about what they had witnessed; a research team and surveillance equipment move in.

timeline.label: CIA publishes the U-2 cover-story admission
timeline.text: Gerald Haines' Studies in Intelligence history states that Blue Book investigators knowingly attributed U-2 sightings to ice crystals and temperature inversions and that 'this led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public.'

timeline.label: DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677 released
timeline.text: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense releases both the Halt memo and the November 1975 Malmstrom overflight records to The Black Vault in a single case.

timeline.label: Wilson's alleged SAP inquiry begins
timeline.text: Per the Davis notes, Joint Staff J-2 Vice Admiral Thomas Wilson - prompted by the Disclosure Project's Washington briefings - begins trying to locate a special access programme holding recovered non-human material.

timeline.label: Bigelow's first NIDS interview
timeline.text: Bigelow tells the Deseret News that anomalous aerial activity and animal deaths have continued around the ranch and that 'we wouldn't be there just for the weather,' while declining to discuss specifics.

timeline.label: Disclosure Project press conference
timeline.text: Steven Greer presents about twenty former military and government witnesses at the National Press Club and demands congressional hearings with subpoena power. Global coverage; no hearing.

timeline.label: CAUS still litigating against DoD
timeline.text: The Ninth Circuit decides Citizens Against UFO Secrecy, Inc. v. United States Department of Defense - twenty-four years after the organisation was founded.

timeline.label: The Wilson-Davis meeting
timeline.text: Eric Davis takes fifteen pages of handwritten notes recording Admiral Thomas Wilson describing being refused access, on need-to-know grounds, to a SAP holding recovered non-human material in contractor custody.

timeline.label: Podesta calls for declassification
timeline.text: Six days after the Wilson meeting, the former White House Chief of Staff appears at the National Press Club for the Coalition for Freedom of Information and demands the government open its UFO files.

timeline.label: NIDS closes; ranch retained
timeline.text: Bigelow shuts the institute but keeps Skinwalker Ranch. The cleared cadre remains intact and available.

timeline.label: DIA contacts Bigelow about Skinwalker
timeline.text: A senior Defense Intelligence Agency official writes to Bigelow about the ranch; Bigelow connects him to Senator Harry Reid. The AAWSAP contract follows in 2008 - the private capability is re-federalised without a new office being created.

timeline.label: Wilson-Davis notes surface
timeline.text: The fifteen pages enter public circulation. Davis confirms the notes are his; Wilson denies the meeting and its substance. No agency has attempted to reconcile the two.

cia-haines-1997.desc: The passage that matters, in full, from the section headed 'CIA's U-2 and OXCART as UFOs': 'The early U-2s were silver (they were later painted black) and reflected the rays from the sun, especially at sunrise and sunset. They often appeared as fiery objects to observers below. Air Force BLUE BOOK investigators aware of the secret U-2 flights tried to explain away such sightings by linking them to natural phenomena such as ice crystals and temperature inversions. By checking with the Agency's U-2 Project Staff in Washington, BLUE BOOK investigators were able to attribute many UFO sightings to U-2 flights. They were careful, however, not to reveal the true cause of the sighting to the public. According to later estimates from CIA officials who worked on the U-2 project and the OXCART (SR-71, or Blackbird) project, over half of all UFO reports from the late 1950s through the 1960s were accounted for by manned reconnaissance flights (namely the U-2) over the United States. This led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public in order to allay public fears and to protect an extraordinarily sensitive national security project. While perhaps justified, this deception added fuel to the later conspiracy theories and the coverup controversy of the 1970s.' The article also records that when pressure built for release of the Robertson Panel report, 'Philip Strong, Deputy Assistant Director of OSI, refused to declassify the report and declined to disclose CIA sponsorship of the panel. As an alternative, the Agency prepared a sanitized version of the report which deleted any reference to CIA and avoided mention of any psychological warfare potential in the UFO controversy.' Note what this establishes and what it does not. It establishes, from the Agency's own historian in the Agency's own journal, that the United States Air Force knowingly issued false explanations for UFO sightings to the American public for at least a decade, and that CIA sanitised a scientific panel report to conceal its own sponsorship and its psychological-warfare interest. It does not establish that every sighting was a U-2. The number given is 'over half,' and it is an estimate by the people with the strongest interest in it being high. The residual - the sightings not accounted for by reconnaissance aircraft, in a period when the Air Force was publicly reporting an unexplained rate falling to four percent - is the part CIA did not address.

aaro-historical-record-vol1.desc: A full-text review of Volume I establishes what the report covers and what it does not. It covers: Project SAUCER, SIGN, GRUDGE (original and reestablished), TWINKLE, BEAR, BLUE BOOK; the CIA Special Study Group, the Robertson Panel and the Durant Report; the O'Brien Committee; the Condon Report; the 1994-97 Roswell Reports; AAWSAP, AATIP, the UAP Task Force, AOIMSG, AOIMEXEC, the UAP Independent Study Team and AARO itself; KONA BLUE; and a long roster of legitimate classified aerospace programmes offered as explanations - Project Mogul, High Dive, Aquatone/Dragon Lady, WS-117L/CORONA, the Avrocar, OXCART/A-12/SR-71, TATTLETALE/GRAB, Poppy, Gambit, Hexagon, HAVE Blue/F-117A, TACIT Blue, the B-2, SDI, GNAT 750, Predator, Reaper, DarkStar, Polecat, Sentinel and Global Hawk. It names Twining, Ruppelt, Vandenberg, Chadwell, Bedell Smith, Robertson, Durant, Cabell, Hynek, Seamans, Condon, Carter, Press, Frosch, Clinton, Berger, Schiff, Reid, Norquist, Clapper, Lynn, O'Brien, Sagan, Bush, Chamberlain, McCone, Widnall, Weaver and McAndrew. It does not name Kirtland AFB, AFOSI, Paul Bennewitz, Richard Doty, Linda Moulton Howe, Project MOON DUST, Operation BLUE FLY, MJ-12, Project AQUARIUS, Rendlesham Forest, RAF Bentwaters or Woodbridge, Charles Halt, Admiral Thomas Wilson, Eric Davis, the Wilson-Davis notes, or the 1975 Loring/Wurtsmith/Malmstrom/Minot overflights. Every one of those omitted items is documented in records the United States government itself has released - the Halt memo and the Malmstrom records through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense under FOIA case 97-F-1677, the Kirtland AFOSI file under FOIA, the NSA withholding through a federal court, the RAAF records destruction through GAO. A historical review that omits the government's own released records on the subject it was commissioned to review is not an incomplete history. It is a selection, and the selection criterion is visible: what is included is what can be attributed to conventional programmes; what is excluded is what cannot.

wilson-davis-memo.desc: What the notes are alleged to contain, and why the board keeps them at claim tier 2 rather than promoting or dismissing them. The document is fifteen pages of handwriting. It is dated 16 October 2002. Its author, Eric W. Davis, is alive, named, and has confirmed authorship. Its subject, Vice Admiral Thomas R. Wilson (ret.), is alive, named, and denies it. The substance recorded is: that in 1997, as Joint Staff J-2, Wilson learned from a colleague of a special access programme concerning recovered non-human material; that he traced it through the SAP oversight apparatus to a programme with an aerospace contractor as the custodian; that he obtained a meeting with the programme's gatekeepers - described as a security officer, a corporate programme manager and a lawyer; and that he was refused the read-on because he had no need to know, notwithstanding his position. Three things make this more than a rumour and less than proof. More: the mechanism it describes - contractor-held custody, access denial to a cleared senior official on need-to-know grounds - was independently described under oath by David Grusch to the House Oversight Committee on 26 July 2023, and Grusch had no access to Wilson. Less: there is no second witness, no corroborating document, and the chain of custody by which the notes reached the public in 2019 has never been established on the record. Neither DoD nor AARO has published anything about the document. Members of the House Intelligence subcommittee put it to Ronald Moultrie and Scott Bray on 17 May 2022 and were told the witnesses were unaware of it. Two men are alive who can settle this, and no institution with subpoena power has attempted to make them.

afosi-kirtland-file.desc: The Bennewitz operation is the only place in this domain where the state's method is documented rather than inferred, and it is worth setting out the sequence precisely. 1979: Paul Bennewitz, a physicist running a USAF-supplying instrumentation company on the eastern edge of Kirtland AFB, begins recording lights and electronic emissions over the Manzano Weapons Storage Area and reports them, in writing, to the Air Force. 10 November 1980: AFOSI generates a record confirming that Kirtland security police have themselves observed unexplained aerial objects in the Coyote Canyon area and noting Bennewitz's activity. That document is the concession. From 1981: rather than investigate its own security police reports, AFOSI - through Special Agent Richard Doty and the civilian researcher Bill Moore - begins supplying Bennewitz with fabricated material about underground alien bases, treaties and biological experimentation, tailored to what he already half-believed. April 1983: Doty runs a parallel operation on a broadcaster, showing Linda Moulton Howe a paper she may read but not copy and promising film that never comes. December 1984: an anonymous film arrives in Los Angeles postmarked Albuquerque, producing the MJ-12 documents. 1988: Bennewitz is hospitalised. July 1989: Moore stands up at a MUFON conference and admits the whole thing. What was protected? Not the truth about aliens; the operation's own content was fiction. The thing protected was whatever was actually generating unexplained objects over a nuclear weapons storage complex - the thing AFOSI's own 10 November 1980 document conceded was happening and which no released record shows anyone ever investigated. Forty-six years later, AARO's historical review does not mention any of it.

caus-v-nsa.desc: The precise posture of the case matters because it is routinely misdescribed in both directions. NSA did not say it had no UFO records; it said it had them and could not release them. The plaintiffs did not lose because their claim was frivolous; they lost because the agency persuaded a judge, in a document the plaintiffs were forbidden to see, that disclosure would damage national security. The affidavit was executed by Eugene F. Yeates as NSA's Chief of Policy. The district court reviewed it in camera and granted summary judgment; the D.C. Circuit affirmed on 3 November 1981; the Supreme Court denied certiorari on 8 March 1982. NSA thereafter released the underlying records in a form that made the point of the litigation vividly: most pages carried only a few visible words, with the excisions made in white-out rather than black ink. A Mandatory Declassification Review filed in July 2013 was required to force further release. The Yeates affidavit itself has since been published in redacted form in NSA's own UFO collection. In 1995, GAO's Roswell records audit listed 'National Security Agency, Fort Meade, Md. - FOIA records, Citizens Against UFO Secrecy' among the record sets it searched, which means a private citizens' FOIA litigation body had become a recognised federal record set. This is the strongest single judicial fact in the American UFO record, and it has never been superseded: the United States holds UFO-related signals intelligence that it has told a federal court it cannot disclose.

yankee-blue.desc: The board's position on YANKEE BLUE is deliberately unresolved, and the reason is instructive. If the Wall Street Journal's June 2025 account is accurate, the Air Force ran, for something on the order of two decades, an institutionalised deception in which personnel were falsely read into a fictitious reverse-engineering programme - which would mean that a substantial share of the insider testimony in this field originates in a disinformation operation, and would simultaneously prove that the US Air Force runs disinformation operations about UFOs on its own people at scale. Either conclusion is damaging to the government. But the paper trail is missing. The Office of the Secretary of Defense searched its Correspondence Management Division and reported no records of the alleged spring 2023 cessation memo (case 25-F-3514, September 2025). It could not locate briefing materials prepared for DNI Avril Haines on the subject (case 25-F-3515, under appeal). AFOSI reported no records of any investigation (case 2025-06002-F). On 1 October 2025 the Pentagon's spokesperson said she could not confirm the memo existed and suggested asking the services. On 15 December 2025 an appellate decision found the CMD-only search inadequate under Oglesby v. U.S. Dep't of Army, 920 F.2d 57 (D.C. Cir. 1990) and remanded. So there are exactly three possibilities and the board holds all three open: the memo exists and the department cannot find its own Secretary-level directives; the memo does not exist and a major newspaper's central sourced claim about Pentagon conduct is unsupported; or the memo exists in a channel FOIA does not reach. The first and third are the concealment thesis. The second is a caution against accepting any account, including a debunking account, without the paper.

gao-roswell-report-1995.desc: GAO's report is the closest thing to a neutral federal referee this subject has ever had, and its findings are narrow, verifiable and damning. It was requested by Rep. Steven Schiff and issued 28 July 1995. GAO searched Air Force, Army, Navy, FBI, CIA, NSA, National Archives and presidential library holdings. It reported: that in 1947 Army regulations required air accident reports to be maintained permanently but that no military service filed a report on the Roswell incident and there was no requirement to report a weather balloon crash; that 'although some of the records concerning Roswell activities had been destroyed, there was no information available regarding when or under what authority the records were destroyed'; that only two government records originating in 1947 were recovered; and, specifically, that 'RAAF administrative records (from Mar. 1945 through Dec. 1949) and RAAF outgoing messages (from Oct. 1946 through Dec. 1949) were destroyed.' The disposition form for that destruction records neither the organisation nor the person responsible, nor the date, nor the authority. In federal records terms that is not an anomaly; it is a defect. Four years and three months of one installation's outgoing message traffic, spanning the exact window in question, eliminated with no accountable authority. GAO also documented that a July 1947 FBI record showed the military had reported an object 'resembling a high-altitude weather balloon' - and that this was one of only two 1947-origin records the entire government could produce.

gaps: AARO Historical Record Report Volume II was promised in Volume I (March 2024) and, as of 12 August 2026, has not been published. The board should track whether Volume II addresses Kirtland/Bennewitz/Doty, MOON DUST/BLUE FLY, Rendlesham, or the Wilson-Davis notes - all omitted from Volume I - and treat continued omission as a finding.

The full unredacted Yeates affidavit (NSA, 1980) remains classified. A fresh Mandatory Declassification Review or a FOIA suit citing the passage of 46 years and the intervening AARO/UAPDA disclosure regime is the single highest-value unfired shot in this domain.

The Wilson-Davis notes have never been the subject of any sworn testimony by either principal. Eric Davis and Thomas Wilson are both alive. A congressional deposition of either would resolve, in one session, the most specific custody allegation in the record. No committee has attempted it.

No primary MOON DUST or BLUE FLY charter document has been located in a public archive. What exists publicly is State Department cable traffic and Air Force correspondence generated in response to congressional and FOIA inquiries. The founding Air Force Intelligence directive establishing the programmes has never surfaced.

The AFOSI Kirtland file is incomplete in the public record. The 10 November 1980 complaint-form entry conceding unexplained objects over Coyote Canyon has no released follow-up investigative file. Either no investigation was opened - which is itself remarkable at a nuclear weapons storage site - or the file has not been released.

John Burroughs' USAF service medical records for December 1980-January 1981 have not been produced. The administrative basis on which the VA granted his claim in 2015 is not public. A Privacy Act/FOIA route through VA with the claimant's consent could establish whether the records were destroyed, misfiled, or withheld.

The NORAD and SAC command-post message traffic for the October-November 1975 Loring, Wurtsmith and Minot incidents is less completely released than the Malmstrom set. A targeted FOIA/MDR to the Air Force Historical Research Agency and NORAD for the command director's logs of 27 Oct - 15 Nov 1975 is a defined, achievable request.

NIDS' raw data from 1996-2004 - Skinwalker Ranch instrument records, necropsy reports, hotline casework - has never been published or independently examined and its disposition after the 2004 shutdown is unknown. If it transferred to BAASS it may now be a federal record subject to FOIA.

The chain of custody by which the Wilson-Davis notes left Eric Davis's possession and entered public circulation in 2019 has never been established. Accounts connect them to material associated with the estate of Edgar Mitchell; that connection is unverified.

No copy of the 'Project AQUARIUS' paper shown to Linda Moulton Howe in April 1983 has ever surfaced in any archive. NARA has confirmed it searched NSC indexes under 'Aquarius' and found nothing. AFOSI's own records of Doty's 1983 activities have not been released.

The 1995 distribution list for 'The Best Available Evidence' has never been published, so it is not possible to establish which officials and heads of state received the Rockefeller Initiative's brief or whether any responded.

Clinton Library FOIA collections 2006-0474-F, 2006-0480-F and 2008-0359-F are described in published finding aids but the underlying documents have not been scanned or made available online. A request to the Clinton Library for digitisation of 2006-0480-F (Clinton-Laurance Rockefeller correspondence) is a concrete next step.

Christopher 'Kit' Green's medical casework on claimed anomalous-injury cases - the human-effects data referenced across the NIDS/BAASS era - has never been released in any form. Its existence rests on his own statements and those of programme participants.

The Yankee Blue FOIA remand of 15 December 2025 is live. The outcome of the Department of War's renewed search is the single most consequential pending records action in this domain and should be tracked to resolution.
